text.p: These are the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan warned the U.N. has already spent time, lives and millions of dollars on Cyprus at the opening ceremony of the direct talks to solve the conflict at Troutbeck, New York, yesterday.
- The government will create a national advisory health council.
- Richard Holbrooke, the U.S. presidential emissary on Cyprus, plays down the expectations of the talks.
- Doctors and the government are on a collision course over demands for better working conditions. The doctors' association describes a government proposal to settle the issue "unacceptable".
- Annan urges the two sides to reach an agreement to settle the Cyprus conflict on the basis of partnership.
- Legislation on regulating television and radio stations will be ready in September.

- Annan submitted a package of proposals to the two leaders at the first day of the Troutbeck talks yesterday. The US undermined the opening ceremony with the conspicuous absence of envoy Carey Cavanaugh, who arrived when the ceremony ended.
- Industrial disputes threaten labour peace in the hotel industry.
- The United Nations appear determined to broker a settlement. Annan sees the talks as the last opportunity for Cyprus.

- Bankers and employees' negotiations on the renewal of collective working agreements are deadlocked. Employees are seeking pay rises, adjustments to working hours, participation on the board of directors of the banks and other fringe benefits.
